title: Water Damage Mitigation Training Note: Weight of Flooring That Stood Wet
content:
**Training note — Water Damage Mitigation tear-out debris**

On a Water Damage Mitigation job's tear-out debris haul-off line, the flooring load size is the number of square feet of removed flooring (the square feet on the job's pad removal and carpet removal lines) that counts as one pickup-truck load.

Flooring that stood wet is heavier per square foot: when the job's opened date is two or more days after its loss date, the flooring load size is 400 square feet per load; when the opened date is exactly one day after the loss date, it is 500 square feet per load; when the job was opened on its loss date, no stood-wet weighting applies.

## Questions answered
**Which dates decide the weighting?** The loss date and the opened date on the job record; the gap between them is counted in calendar days.

**What if the crew was booked three days after the loss?** Three days is two or more days, so the flooring load size is 400 square feet per load.

**And a booking the day after the loss?** Exactly one day: 500 square feet per load.

**And a booking the same day as the loss?** No stood-wet weighting applies to the flooring load size.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical loss on the 1st of a month)
| Opened on | Days after the loss | Flooring load size under this rule |
|---|---|---|
| the 1st | 0 | no stood-wet weighting |
| the 2nd | 1 | 500 square feet per load |
| the 3rd | 2 | 400 square feet per load |
| the 9th | 8 | 400 square feet per load |
